data.title: Geographic Impossibility Login
data.description: Detects login attempts from geographically impossible locations within a short timeframe. When a user authenticates from one country and a second authentication occurs from a distant country within a window that makes physical travel impossible, it strongly indicates credential compromise and concurrent use by an attacker.

queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Geographic Impossibility Login")`
`comment("Aggregation that cannot be expressed in Sigma")`
`comment("Original condition: selection | near by user_id | where geo_distance(src.geo_lat, src.geo_lon, dst.geo_lat, dst.geo_lon) > 1000 and time_diff < 60m")`
index=flame_banking sourcetype=flame:auth_logs (event_type="login_success" OR event_type="login_attempt")
| transaction user_id maxspan=60m
| where eventcount >= 2

falsepositives: Users employing VPN services that change egress country between sessions
Corporate proxy chains routing through geographically distributed data centers
